units: Targ. Gen. I, 2; a. v. fr.—With suffixes of pers. pron. מִנִּי, מִי׳ from me; מִנָּךְ, מִי׳ from thee; מִנֵּיה, מִי׳ from him, it &c. Ib. XXII, 12. Ib. III, 3; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:4:12">Y. Ber. II, 5ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>מן הן דסלק</he> to where he had come from.
<cite ref="Shabbat 80b:5">Sabb. 80ᵇ</cite> <he>מן דיליה דא ליה</he> this came to him from his own doing.
<cite ref="Sotah 40a:7">Sot. 40ᵃ</cite> <he>ומאי נפקא ליך מִינָּהּ</he> and what difference does it make? <he>מִנִּי ומִנֵּיה יתקלס וכ׳</he> through myself and him the Most High is exalted.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 18a:8">B. Kam. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>קאזיל מיניה מיניה</he> it was lost through its (the chicken’s) action alone.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7:3:18">Y. Peah VII, 20ᵇ</cite> <he>מיניה וביה הוא</he> (the sweetness) is entirely its own (no honey has been added).
Snh. 39ᵇ, v. אִבָּא; a. fr.—לא כולא מיניה, לא כל כמיניה it is not at all in his power; v. כּוֹלָא.—מן ד־ from the time that, after; from the fact that; when; because.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2:14">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite> <he>מן דאכלון</he> after they had eaten; a. v. fr.; v. <cite ref="M00230"><he>מִדְּ־</he></cite>.
